mainTopic: Laws of the חליצה shoe: intention, material, the meaning of חלץ, and the status of an אנפיליא
overview: The גמרא first confirms that people really do wear one shoe over another, since רב יהודה once went out in five layers. Next, רב rules that a young יבמה who grew up among the brothers may marry one of them, and the גמרא gives two readings of whether a sandal pulled off without intention matters. רב then teaches that a חליצה shoe must be leather, learned from תחש, though any leather works because the word נעל is repeated. A leather shoe with hair straps is fine, but an all-hair one is only a slipper. The גמרא proves from the words 'מעל רגלו' that חליצה means pulling the shoe off, even though the root חלץ can also mean strengthening. In a side story, רבן גמליאל answers a heretic who claimed ה׳ did חליצה from Israel. Finally, the גמרא resolves conflicting sources about the אנפיליא: a leather one counts as a shoe and a cloth one does not. A ברייתא supporting this begins at the end of the amud, and its ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do people really wear one shoe on top of another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the case just discussed, a shoe worn over another shoe, ever really happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask whether the case it was just talking about happens in real life. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion dealt with חליצה done on a shoe worn over another shoe. Before going further, the גמרא checks that this is a real situation and not just a made-up one.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there really...? (a question about whether something exists)

phrases.english: And is there really a case like this?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the case just before, where one shoe is worn on top of another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about a shoe on top of a shoe.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the case of wearing one shoe over another actually happens.

steps.title: Yes, רב יהודה once wore five layers of shoes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes: the רבנן saw רב יהודה go to the market wearing five pairs of slippers, one on top of another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. The רבנן saw רב יהודה go out to the market in five pairs of slippers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this really happens. It proves it with a story the רבנן saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה wore several layers of soft shoes at once. So wearing one shoe over another is a real-life situation.

phrases.english: Yes, for the Sages saw Rav Yehuda
who went out wearing five pairs of slippers to the market.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רב יהודה was seen wearing five layered pairs of slippers.

steps.title: A young יבמה who grew up among the brothers may marry one of them
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a יבמה who grew up while living among the brothers may do יבום with one of them. We do not worry that she pulled off a sandal from one of them and so already did חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A יבמה who grew up among the brothers may marry one of them. We do not worry that she took off a sandal from one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule is brought. A girl who became a יבמה while young and grew up around the brothers may still marry one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children often pull shoes off people while playing. Someone might worry that she did this to one of the brothers and that it counted as חליצה, which would forbid her to all of them. רב says we do not worry about this.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow whose husband died without children, waiting for יבום or חליצה
she removed a sandal (the act of חליצה)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A yevama who grew up among the brothers
is permitted to marry one of the brothers,
and we are not concerned that perhaps she removed
a sandal from one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about חליצה done without intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה who grew up among the brothers may do יבום. We do not worry that she already did חליצה with one of them.

steps.title: Reading רב closely: only because we did not see it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from רב's wording that she is allowed only because nobody saw her pull off a sandal. If we did see it, we would worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that we did not see it. But if we did see it, we would worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רב's words closely and finds a hidden rule in them. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said we do not worry that she 'perhaps' did it. That sounds like it is only a doubt. So it seems that if we actually saw her pull off a brother's sandal, it would count as חליצה and she would be forbidden to the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason is (used to start a close reading)

phrases.english: The reason is that we did not see it,
but if we did see it, we would be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a hidden rule out of רב's statement in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From רב's wording: if we saw her remove a sandal, it would count against her.

steps.title: But חליצה needs both sides to intend it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חליצה is invalid unless both the man and the woman intend it. So how could a child playing with a sandal count?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if he intended and she did not, or she intended and he did not, the חליצה is invalid. Both of them must intend it together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the close reading from step 4. It uses a ברייתא that says חליצה without intention does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young girl pulling off a sandal in play has no intention to do חליצה, and neither does the brother. According to the ברייתא, that act is meaningless. So why would seeing it make any difference?

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא (starts a challenge)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנִּתְכַּוֵּון הוּא וְלֹא נִתְכַּוְּונָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Whether he intended and she did not intend,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנִּתְכַּוְּונָה הִיא וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון הוּא —
phrases.english: or whether she intended and he did not intend,
her halitza is invalid,
unless both of them intend it as one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the close reading made in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a sandal we saw her remove would count against her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חליצה needs intention from both sides. A child's playful act has no intention, so it should mean nothing even if seen.

steps.title: רב meant: even if we saw it, we do not worry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב: even if we saw her pull off a sandal, we do not worry that they intended it as חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: even if we saw it, we do not worry that they had intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing how we read רב. The close reading from step 4 is dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's 'we do not worry' now means: even when we saw it happen, we do not suspect that they intended חליצה. Without intention the act is nothing. So רב fully agrees with the ברייתא.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Even though we saw it,
we are not concerned that perhaps they intended it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by rereading רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's words implied that a sandal we saw her remove would count against her.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if we saw it, the act means nothing, because we assume there was no intention.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, a sandal pulled off without intention does nothing at all, even if everyone saw it.

steps.title: Second version: if we saw it, we do worry
steps.stepSummary: Others keep the close reading: she is allowed only because nobody saw it. If we did see her remove a sandal, we worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: the reason is that we did not see it. But if we saw it, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the discussion. This version keeps the close reading that the first version dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version says that seeing her remove a sandal really does matter, even without intention. It now has to explain how this fits with the ברייתא that requires intention. That comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (introduces a second version)

steps.confusionAlert: The words of this inference are the same as in step 4. The difference is that here the גמרא keeps the inference instead of rereading רב.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
The reason is that we did not see it,
but if we did see it, we are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of how to read רב, opposite to step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If we saw her remove a brother's sandal, we treat it as affecting her status.

steps.title: Intention is needed to free her, but not to forbid her to the brothers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's need for intention applies only to freeing her to marry someone else. Even without intention, the act is enough to forbid her to the brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא that requires intention means that it is needed to permit her to marry anyone. But to become forbidden to the brothers, she is disqualified even without it.
steps.whatsHappening: The second version explains how its reading fits with the ברייתא. It splits חליצה into two different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה does two things: it frees her to marry an outsider, and it forbids her to the brothers. Freeing her needs full intention. Forbidding her to the brothers happens even through an act without intention.

keyTerms.meaning: to become permitted to the world, meaning to marry an outsider

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: a sandal pulled off without intention does nothing. Version 2: without intention it cannot free her to marry others, but it still forbids her to the brothers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that חליצה has two separate results, and that each one can need a different level of intention.

phrases.english: And that which was taught, that intention is required,
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא quoted in step 5.

phrases.english: that applies to becoming permitted to marry anyone,
but for the brothers she is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the second version against the ברייתא from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that חליצה without intention does nothing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Intention is needed only to free her to marry outsiders. An act without intention still forbids her to the brothers.

steps.title: A sandal sewn with flax cannot be used for this
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: you cannot do חליצה with a sandal stitched with flax, because the פסוק describes a shoe as תחש (animal skin).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A sandal sewn with flax may not be used for חליצה, because it says 'and I shod you with תחש.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב about what a valid חליצה shoe must be made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל speaks of a shoe made of תחש, which is animal leather. רב learns from this that a shoe means something made of leather, so even the stitching cannot be plant material like flax.

keyTerms.meaning: Sandal; the shoe used for חליצה
An animal whose skin was used as leather

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A sandal sewn with flax —
one may not perform חליצה with it,
as it says: 'And I shod you with תחש.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the material of the חליצה shoe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sandal stitched with flax is invalid for חליצה, since a shoe must be leather like תחש.

steps.title: Maybe only תחש leather works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes: if the source is תחש, maybe only תחש leather is valid and nothing else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: תחש, yes; anything else, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's source by reading it too strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק names one specific animal, maybe the rule is limited to that animal's leather. Then even ordinary cow or goat leather would be invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But let us say: תחש — yes,
anything else — no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of רב's source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק naming one animal should limit the rule to that animal only.

steps.title: The repeated word נעל widens the rule
steps.stepSummary: The word נעל appears again and again, and that repetition includes other kinds of leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Shoe,' 'shoe' — the Torah included more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the repeated word 'shoe' in the Torah widens the rule beyond תחש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the Torah keeps saying נעל, we learn that more than just תחש is included. So all leather shoes are valid.

phrases.english: 'Shoe,' 'shoe' — it included more.
phrases.notes: The word נעל comes up several times in the Torah's section about חליצה, and each extra mention adds more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional פסוק source that widens the rule
steps.terutzMaskana: All leather is valid because of the repeated נעל.

steps.title: Then why not every material?
steps.stepSummary: If the repeated נעל widens the rule, maybe it should include shoes of any material at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If 'shoe,' 'shoe' included more, then it should include everything too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now pushes the other way: maybe the widening is too wide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we say the repetition adds more, why stop at leather? Maybe a shoe of any material, even flax, should be valid. That would contradict רב's rule.

phrases.english: If 'shoe,' 'shoe' included more,
then even all things too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The widening from the repeated נעל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the repetition widens the rule, there is no clear reason to stop at leather.

steps.title: Otherwise the word תחש would teach nothing
steps.stepSummary: If every material were included, the word תחש would be pointless, so it must limit the rule to leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does 'תחש' accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word תחש must still teach something: the shoe has to be leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources work together. נעל widens the rule beyond תחש to all leather, and תחש keeps it limited to leather, so non-leather like flax is out.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it accomplish? What is it for?

steps.whatToRemember: A חליצה shoe must be leather (from תחש), but any kind of leather works (from the repeated נעל).

phrases.english: If so, 'תחש' —
what does it accomplish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only leather is valid; תחש sets that limit.

steps.title: A leather shoe with hair straps
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks רב about a shoe made of leather whose strap parts are made of hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked רב: If the shoe is leather but its strap parts are hair, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question about a mixed shoe: leather body, hair straps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hair comes from an animal but is not leather. רבי אלעזר wants to know if those hair parts ruin the shoe, the way flax stitching did.

keyTerms.meaning: Its strap parts (the parts that hold the straps)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked Rav:
If it is made of leather,
and its strap parts are of hair, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the leather rule to a mixed case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a leather shoe with hair strap parts count for חליצה?

steps.title: It still counts as a תחש shoe
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that such a shoe is still called a shoe of תחש, so it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Don't we still call it 'I shod you with תחש'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the shoe is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hair comes from an animal, so the shoe still fits the description of a תחש shoe. Flax is different because it comes from a plant.

keyTerms.meaning: We apply the פסוק to it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי לָא קָרֵינַן בֵּיהּ
phrases.english: He said to him: Do we not apply to it
'And I shod you with תחש'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי לָא קָרֵינַן בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Valid, since it is still a shoe from animal material.

steps.title: Then an all-hair shoe should work too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if animal hair is fine, a shoe made completely of hair should also be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a shoe made entirely of hair should also be valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's reasoning by taking it one step further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If what matters is that the material comes from an animal, then hair alone should be enough. The גמרא is checking how far this logic goes.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כּוּלּוֹ שֶׁל שֵׂעָר נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, one made entirely of hair too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כּוּלּוֹ שֶׁל שֵׂעָר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's answer that hair parts are fine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If animal origin is enough, an all-hair shoe should also be valid.

steps.title: An all-hair shoe is called a slipper
steps.stepSummary: A shoe made completely of hair is not called a shoe at all; it is called a slipper.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one is called a slipper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an all-hair item is not a shoe in name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not only the material but whether the item is called a נעל. A leather shoe with hair straps is still a shoe, but something made only of hair is a slipper.
steps.whatToRemember: A leather shoe with some hair parts is valid, but an all-hair foot covering is a slipper and does not count.

phrases.english: That one is called a slipper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different category of object by name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal material makes a valid shoe.
steps.terutzMaskana: An all-hair item is a slipper, not a shoe.

steps.title: How do we know וחלצה means removing?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks שמואל how we know that the word וחלצה in the פסוק means pulling off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to שמואל: How do we know that 'And she shall remove his shoe from on his foot' means pulling off?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question about the meaning of the key word in the חליצה פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חלץ can have more than one meaning. רב כהנא wants a source showing that here it means taking the shoe off.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to Shmuel:
From where do we know that this
'and she shall remove his shoe from on his foot'
means pulling off?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל: מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the meaning of the word חליצה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the word וחלצה means removing.

steps.title: Proof from the stones with נגע
steps.stepSummary: The same word is used for taking out stones with נגע from a house, where it clearly means removing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they shall remove the stones in which the נגע is.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer brings a פסוק where the same word clearly means taking something out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a house that has נגע, the stones are pulled out of the wall. Since the same word is used there, it shows that חלץ means removing.

keyTerms.meaning: A spiritual skin-type mark, here on a house

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And they shall remove the stones
in which the נגע is.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same word is used for removing stones, so it means removing.
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of וחלצה as removing

steps.title: Maybe the word means strengthening, as in arming soldiers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that חלץ could mean strengthening, based on the פסוק about arming men for war.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the word means strengthening, as the פסוק says: 'Arm men from among you for the army.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from the last step. It brings a פסוק where the same root seems to mean making men strong and ready for battle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חלץ can mean strengthening, then וחלצה might mean the woman tightens the shoe on his foot, not takes it off. That would change how חליצה is done. So the proof from the house with נגע is no longer enough.

keyTerms.meaning: arm yourselves, get ready (from the root חלץ)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of חלץ: 'take off / remove' and 'make strong'. The whole סוגיא is about which meaning fits חליצה.

phrases.english: But say it is a term of strengthening,
as it is written:
"Arm men from among you for the army!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the meaning 'removing' that was proven in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that וחלצה means pulling off.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק uses the same root to mean arming or strengthening, so וחלצה could mean tightening the shoe.

steps.title: Arming soldiers also means taking them out
steps.stepSummary: Even in the army פסוק, the word means taking men out of their homes to go to war.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it means taking them out of their houses to go to battle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the army פסוק also means removing. The men are pulled out of their homes and sent to war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not accept that this פסוק means strengthening. It reads it with the same meaning as before, removing. So the meaning 'pulling off' still stands.

phrases.english: There too,
it means taking out from the house to battle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The army פסוק uses חלץ to mean strengthening.
steps.terutzMaskana: It also means removing: taking men out of their homes.

steps.title: A challenge from the פסוק about the poor man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in איוב that seems to say the poor man is strengthened through his suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'He delivers the poor man through his affliction.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק that seems to use חלץ as strengthening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'בעניו', 'through' his affliction, not 'from' his affliction. That sounds like the suffering makes him stronger, not that he is taken out of it. So again חלץ seems to mean strengthening.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"He delivers the poor man through his affliction!"
phrases.notes: איוב 36:15. The word 'through' is what makes it sound like strengthening, not rescuing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חלץ means removing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Through his affliction' suggests the poor man is made strong by suffering, not taken out of it.

steps.title: His suffering earns him rescue from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means that, as a reward for his suffering, ה׳ saves him from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a reward for his affliction, He will rescue him from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading 'בעניו' as 'because of his affliction'. The word חלץ still means taking out, rescuing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בעניו' does not describe what he is taken out of. It describes what earns him the rescue. He is pulled out of the punishment of גיהנם, so חלץ still means removing.

phrases.english: As a reward for his affliction,
He will rescue him from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Through his affliction' means he is strengthened by suffering.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means he is rescued (taken out) from גיהנם as a reward for suffering.

steps.title: A challenge from the angel who protects those who fear ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in תהלים that seems to say the angel strengthens those who fear ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the פסוק: 'The angel of ה׳ camps around those who fear Him, and וַיְחַלְּצֵם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third פסוק where חלץ seems to mean strengthening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An angel camping around people sounds like protection and giving them strength. So וַיְחַלְּצֵם might mean 'He strengthens them', not 'He takes them out'.

keyTerms.meaning: but what about this that is written

phrases.english: But what about that which is written:
"The angel of ה׳ camps around those who fear Him
and delivers them!"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דִּכְתִיב חֹנֶה מַלְאַךְ ה׳ סָבִיב לִירֵאָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further challenge after step 23's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חלץ means removing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Protection by an angel suggests strengthening, so חלץ there seems to mean strengthening.

steps.title: Those who fear ה׳ are rescued from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: Same answer as before: as a reward for fearing ה׳, they are saved from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a reward for fearing Him, He will rescue them from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as in step 23. The word still means taking out, rescuing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people who fear ה׳ are pulled out of the punishment of גיהנם. So this פסוק also fits the meaning 'removing'.

phrases.english: As a reward for those who fear Him,
He will rescue them from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 the same way step 23 answered step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: וַיְחַלְּצֵם means the angel strengthens them.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means they are rescued from גיהנם as a reward.

steps.title: A challenge from 'He will strengthen your bones'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in ישעיהו that רבא explains clearly as strengthening the bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the פסוק 'וְעַצְמֹתֶיךָ יַחֲלִיץ'? רבי אלעזר said this is the best of all blessings, and רבא said it means strengthening of the bones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth פסוק, and this time an אמורא openly explains חלץ as strengthening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the earlier answers will not work. רבא directly says the word means making the bones strong. So we have clear proof that חלץ can mean strengthening.

keyTerms.meaning: and He will strengthen your bones

phrases.english: But what about that which is written:
"And He will strengthen your bones,"
and Rabbi Elazar said:
This is the best of the blessings,
and Rava said: It means strengthening of the bones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The strongest challenge, after the previous ones were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חלץ means removing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא explicitly explains this פסוק as strengthening, so the root clearly can mean strengthening.

steps.title: The word can mean both, but here it must mean pulling off
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees חלץ can mean both things, but the חליצה פסוק says 'from on his foot', which only fits taking off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, the word can mean this and can mean that. But here, if you think it means strengthening, then the תורה should have written 'she shall strengthen his shoe on his foot'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the root has two meanings. Then it proves from the wording of the חליצה פסוק that here it means taking off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real פסוק says 'מעל רגלו', 'from on his foot'. If the meaning were tightening, the תורה would have written 'ברגלו', 'on his foot'. The word 'from' shows the shoe is being removed.

keyTerms.meaning: it can mean this and it can mean that

steps.whatToRemember: The root חלץ can mean both removing and strengthening. In חליצה it means pulling the shoe off, because the תורה says 'from on his foot'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles that the מצוה of חליצה is taking the shoe off, not tightening it.

phrases.english: Yes, it means this and it means that.
But here, if it would enter your mind
that it means strengthening,
if so, the Merciful One should have written
"And she shall strengthen his shoe on his foot"!
phrases.notes: The real פסוק says מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ, 'from on his foot', which only fits taking the shoe off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by admitting the point and then proving the meaning from the context.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession plus proof from the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חלץ can mean strengthening, וחלצה might mean tightening the shoe.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the פסוק says 'from on his foot', וחלצה here must mean pulling off.

steps.title: Maybe 'From on His Foot' Teaches Even the Calf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the words 'מעל רגלו' might not prove removal. They could teach that the shoe may be tightened even on the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written only 'on his foot', I would have thought tightening counts on the foot but not on the calf. So the תורה wrote 'from on his foot' to include even the calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from the last step. It offers another way to read 'מעל רגלו' that still fits the idea that חלץ means tightening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 the גמרא said 'מעל רגלו' only makes sense if חלץ means taking off. Here it argues that 'מעל' could instead stretch the area upward, so tightening counts even on the calf, which is part of the leg. If that is right, the proof for removal falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
From on his foot, the actual wording of the פסוק

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had written "on his foot,"
I would have said: "on his foot", yes,
on his calf, no;
so the Merciful One wrote "from on his foot"
to teach that it counts even on his calf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from 'מעל רגלו' given in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'מעל רגלו' only fits removing the shoe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'מעל' could widen the area to include the calf, which still fits tightening.

steps.title: The Wording Proves חליצה Means Taking Off
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה meant 'even on the calf', it would have written 'במעל רגלו'. Since it wrote 'מעל רגלו', חליצה must mean removing the shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should have written 'on the upper part of his foot'. Why does it say 'from on his foot'? Learn from this that it means pulling the shoe off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge and settles the question: חליצה here means taking the shoe off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To say 'on the area above the foot', the natural wording would be 'במעל רגלו', with the letter ב meaning 'on'. The actual word 'מעל' means 'from on', which describes something coming off. So the challenge fails, and the meaning of removal is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: On the upper part of his foot
Learn from it, a conclusion formula

steps.whatToRemember: חליצה means the יבמה pulls the shoe off the יבם's foot. We learn this from the word 'מעל' ('from on') in the פסוק.

phrases.english: If so, let the Merciful One write "on the upper part of his foot."
What is the meaning of "from on his foot"?
Learn from it that it means pulling off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 and closes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise wording: the תורה would have used a different word for the other meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מעל רגלו' might mean tightening is allowed even on the calf.
steps.terutzMaskana: For that meaning the תורה would write 'במעל רגלו', so 'מעל רגלו' means removal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חליצה is done by removing the shoe.

steps.title: A Heretic Claims ה׳ Did חליצה From Israel
steps.stepSummary: A heretic tells רבן גמליאל that ה׳ has 'done חליצה' from the Jewish people and left them. He brings a פסוק in הושע as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heretic said to רבן גמליאל: You are a nation whose Master has pulled away from you, as the פסוק says, 'With their flocks and herds they will go to seek ה׳ but not find Him; He has withdrawn (חלץ) from them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a side story that uses the word חלץ. A heretic uses a פסוק to insult the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heretic reads 'חלץ מהם' as ה׳ doing a kind of חליצה, like a יבם cutting ties with his יבמה. His point is that ה׳ has broken off His bond with Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: The נשיא, leader of the Jewish people, in his time
He withdrew from them, or he did חליצה from them

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: A certain heretic said to Rabban Gamliel:
You are a nation whose Master has done חליצה from them,
phrases.notes: He means ה׳ has cut ties with you, the way a יבם separates from his יבמה through חליצה.

phrases.english: as it is written: "With their flocks and with their herds they shall go
to seek ה׳, but they shall not find Him;
He has withdrawn from them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side story connected only by the word חלץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The heretic claims, based on הושע 5:6, that ה׳ has abandoned Israel.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: A Backwards חליצה Means Nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל points out that the פסוק says 'חלץ מהם' and not 'חלץ להם'. That means Israel pulled away from ה׳, and a backwards חליצה like that has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Fool, does it say 'He did חליצה to them'? It says 'from them'. And if the brothers-in-law took the shoe off the יבמה, does that mean anything?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers the heretic by reading the exact wording of the פסוק. He shows that the bond between ה׳ and Israel is not broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חלץ להם' would mean ה׳ did חליצה to them. 'חלץ מהם' means they did it to Him, so the people are the ones pulling away. In real חליצה the woman removes the man's shoe. If the men removed hers, it would mean nothing, so Israel's pulling away cannot end the relationship.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבן גמליאל as agreeing that ה׳ left. His point is that the people were the ones pulling away, and that kind of reversed חליצה has no legal effect.

phrases.english: He said to him: Fool,
is it written "He did חליצה to them"?
It is written "חלץ from them",
and if a יבמה had her shoe removed by the brothers-in-law,
phrases.notes: This is backwards. In real חליצה, she takes off his shoe, not the other way around.

phrases.english: is there anything of substance in it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שׁוֹטֶה, מִי כְּתִיב ״חָלַץ לָהֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the heretic's claim from step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise wording of the פסוק ('מהם' and not 'להם').
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ה׳ did חליצה and left Israel.
steps.terutzMaskana: Israel pulled away from ה׳, and a reversed חליצה has no effect.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how close reading of one small word in a פסוק can answer a big challenge to Jewish faith.

steps.title: Is a Soft Cloth Shoe Not Considered a Shoe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says חליצה done with an אנפיליא is invalid. It asks whether this means an אנפיליא is not a shoe at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: with a soft cloth shoe, her חליצה is invalid. Is this saying that an אנפיליא is not a shoe?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and draws a possible conclusion from its words. This line is setting up the next move, where this idea will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה makes חליצה with an אנפיליא invalid, the simple reason would be that it does not count as a מנעל. The גמרא states this idea so it can check it against other sources.

keyTerms.meaning: A soft shoe made of cloth
Is this to say, drawing a conclusion

phrases.english: With a soft cloth shoe, her חליצה is invalid, etc.
Is this to say that a soft cloth shoe is not a shoe?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to analyzing the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's ruling means an אנפיליא does not have the status of a shoe.

steps.title: A משנה in שקלים also shows that an אנפיליא is not a shoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about the תורם, the person who takes coins from the Temple chamber. The משנה lists an אנפיליא separately from a shoe, which suggests it is not a shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned in a משנה: The one who takes the coins from the chamber may not go in wearing a cuffed garment or an אנפיליא. It goes without saying that he may not wear a shoe or sandal, because nobody may enter the Temple courtyard in a shoe or sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from another משנה that an אנפיליא is not a real shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the תורם may not wear an אנפיליא, and then says 'needless to say' a shoe or sandal. If an אנפיליא were a shoe, it would already be forbidden in the עזרה for everyone. Since the משנה needs a special reason to forbid it for the תורם, an אנפיליא must not be a shoe.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who takes coins out of the Temple chamber
A garment with cuffs or folds
A soft foot covering, like a sock or slipper

steps.confusionAlert: The תורם may not wear an אנפיליא for a special reason only (he could hide coins in it). That is exactly why it proves an אנפיליא is not a shoe: a shoe is forbidden in the עזרה for everyone.

phrases.english: And we also learned: the one who takes the funds may not enter
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שקלים 3:2, about the person who takes the shekel coins out of the Temple chamber.

phrases.english: not in a cuffed garment
phrases.notes: Coins could be hidden in it, and people might suspect him of stealing.

phrases.english: and not in an anpileya,
and needless to say, not in a shoe or sandal,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין נִכְנָסִין בְּמִנְעָל וְסַנְדָּל לָעֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: because one may not enter the Temple courtyard in a shoe or sandal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the suggestion in step 32 that an אנפיליא is not a shoe.
steps.raayaObject: That an אנפיליא is not a shoe
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה שקלים 3:2 on the תורם, which lists אנפיליא separately from shoes forbidden in the עזרה

steps.title: A ברייתא about יום הכיפורים treats an אנפיליא like a shoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that groups the אנפיליא together with shoes and sandals as forbidden on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: The rule is the same for a shoe, a sandal and an אנפיליא. One may not walk in them on יום הכיפורים, not even from house to house or from bed to bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that an אנפיליא is not a shoe, using a ברייתא about יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים wearing shoes is forbidden. This ברייתא lists the אנפיליא right next to the shoe and sandal and forbids all three, so it seems an אנפיליא does count as a shoe. That contradicts the משנה in step 33.

phrases.english: And they contradicted it: the same for a shoe, a sandal, and an anpileya,
one may not walk in them,
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is talking about יום הכיפורים, when wearing shoes is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִבַּיִת לְבַיִת וְלֹא מִמִּטָּה לְמִטָּה!
phrases.english: not from house to house and not from bed to bed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the proof in step 33 with a source treating an אנפיליא as a shoe.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an אנפיליא is not a shoe
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום הכיפורים only shoes are forbidden, yet the ברייתא forbids an אנפיליא, so it must be a shoe.

steps.title: אביי: the יום הכיפורים case has padding and is forbidden because of pleasure
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the אנפיליא forbidden on יום הכיפורים is padded, and it is forbidden because it gives pleasure, not because it is a shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is talking about one with padding inside, and it is forbidden because of the pleasure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by explaining the יום הכיפורים ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, an אנפיליא really is not a shoe. The padded kind is still forbidden on יום הכיפורים because it is comfortable, and on that day we are supposed to afflict ourselves.

phrases.english: Abaye said: where it has padding inside,
and it is forbidden because of pleasure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason for the prohibition (pleasure, not shoe status)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids an אנפיליא because it is a shoe.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden only when padded, because of the pleasure.

steps.title: רבא rejects אביי: comfort alone is not forbidden on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether something that is not a shoe is ever forbidden just for comfort. He points out that רבה בר רב הונא wrapped a cloth on his feet and went out on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Is something that is not a shoe forbidden on יום הכיפורים just because of comfort? But רבה בר רב הונא used to wrap a scarf around his feet and go out!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If non-shoes were forbidden because of comfort, then wrapping a soft scarf on the feet should also be forbidden. Yet רבה בר רב הונא did exactly that on יום הכיפורים. So comfort alone is not a reason to forbid footwear that is not a shoe.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But because of pleasure, something that is not a shoe
is it forbidden on Yom Kippur?
But Rabba bar Rav Huna
would wrap a scarf on his feet and go out!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וּמִשּׁוּם תַּעֲנוּג בְּלֹא מִנְעָל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מִי אֲסִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer from step 35.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's whole explanation (pleasure as the reason)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Non-shoe foot coverings are not forbidden for comfort, as shown by רבה בר רב הונא's practice.

steps.title: רבא: a leather אנפיליא is a shoe, a cloth one is not
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own answer: the two sources speak about different kinds of אנפיליא, one made of leather and one made of cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: There is no difficulty. Here it is a leather אנפיליא, and there it is a cloth אנפיליא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the contradiction between the משנה and the יום הכיפורים ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אנפיליא made of leather counts as a shoe, so it is forbidden on יום הכיפורים. One made of cloth is not a shoe, which fits the משנה about the תורם. Each source is talking about a different material.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each source speaks about a different case)

steps.whyThisMatters: The status of footwear depends on its material. Leather is what makes something a shoe for יום הכיפורים, and this also connects back to whether חליצה with an אנפיליא works.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: it is not difficult,
here it is an anpileya of leather,
there it is an anpileya of cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new answer to step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All אנפיליא are the same, so the sources contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leather אנפיליא is a shoe; cloth אנפיליא is not.

steps.title: It makes sense: otherwise two יום הכיפורים sources would contradict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבא's answer. Another ברייתא allows walking at home in אנפילין on יום הכיפורים, which clashes with the first ברייתא unless we split between leather and cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical. If you do not say this, one source about יום הכיפורים contradicts another source about יום הכיפורים. For a ברייתא teaches: A person may not walk in slippers in his house, but he may walk in אנפילין in his house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבא's answer from a second ברייתא about יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא forbids an אנפיליא on יום הכיפורים, but this one allows it. Without רבא's split, these two ברייתות about the very same day would contradict each other. That shows רבא's answer is needed anyway.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
for if you do not say so,
Yom Kippur contradicts Yom Kippur.
For it was taught: a person may not walk
in slippers inside his house,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְטַיֵּיל הוּא בְּאַנְפִּילִין בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ!
phrases.english: but he may walk in anpilin inside his house!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer from step 37.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's split between leather and cloth אנפיליא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא permitting אנפילין at home on יום הכיפורים, which otherwise contradicts the ברייתא in step 34

steps.title: Conclusion: leather אנפיליא versus cloth אנפיליא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the only way to fit the sources together is that one speaks about a leather אנפיליא and the other about a cloth one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this: here it is a leather אנפיליא and there a cloth אנפיליא? Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up and accepts רבא's distinction as proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both ברייתות are about יום הכיפורים, the difference between them must be the material. The forbidding ברייתא means leather, and the permitting ברייתא means cloth. The גמרא confirms this with 'שמע מינה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that

steps.whatToRemember: A leather אנפיליא counts as a shoe (forbidden on יום הכיפורים). A cloth אנפיליא does not count as a shoe (allowed on יום הכיפורים, and not forbidden in the עזרה).

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this:
here it is an anpileya of leather,
there it is an anpileya of cloth?
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the proof in step 38.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Leather אנפיליא has the status of a shoe; cloth אנפיליא does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists unusual footwear for חליצה, including a leather אנפיליא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבא. It lists unusual footwear used for חליצה, such as a torn shoe, a broken sandal, a cork sandal, an amputee's wooden foot, a felt shoe, a stump covering and a leather אנפיליא. It also mentions a woman who does חליצה with an adult יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that fits רבא's view: If she did חליצה with a shoe whose seams opened but still covers most of the foot, or with a broken sandal that still holds most of the foot, or with a sandal made of cork or tree fibers, or with an amputee's wooden foot, or with a felt shoe, or with a stump covering, or with a leather אנפיליא, and a woman who does חליצה with an adult...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's answer. The ברייתא starts listing unusual kinds of footwear, and it specifically says a leather אנפיליא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said there are two kinds of אנפיליא: leather and cloth. This ברייתא names a leather אנפיליא in its list of footwear for חליצה, so it treats leather as a real shoe. That fits רבא's split, because a cloth one would not be treated the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports his view
The ceremony of removing the יבם's shoe that frees the widow from יבום
A shoe whose seams have come apart
A sandal that is broken or partly missing
A wooden foot used by someone missing a leg
A padded covering an amputee puts on the stumps of his legs

steps.whatToRemember: A leather אנפיליא is counted together with real shoes, which supports רבא's split between leather and cloth.
steps.confusionAlert: The list is not finished here. The ברייתא's ruling on all these cases comes right after the list, so do not stop reading at 'מן הגדול'.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבא:
phrases.notes: This backs up רבא's answer just before: one source means a leather אנפיליא, the other a cloth one.

steps.raayaObject: רבא's answer that the sources speak about a leather אנפיליא versus a cloth one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about חליצה that lists a leather אנפיליא together with other kinds of footwear.
